title: SSP-2.1 — Project State Producer Evidence
summary: record the accepted folder-centred producer, versioned lookup, real-data reconciliation, failure retention and focused verification
content_html:
SSP-2.1 — Project State Producer Evidence

Outcome

SSP-2.1 is complete at its review gate. docs_project_state.py owns one server-side full reconciliation that scans the immediate children of projects/, validates matching Projects subject receipts and exact collections, reads canonical Works and Series through the existing catalogue source owner, returns one docs_project_state_report_v1 response, and atomically publishes the matching docs_project_state_folder_lookup_v1 under var/docs/project-state/folder-lookup.json. Both products carry the same content generation and subject generation.

Subsequent decision: this evidence records the product exactly as SSP-2.1 shipped it. Resolver Tokens were later retired before implementation, so SSP-2.6 removes the persisted lookup and its dedicated freshness/status machinery while retaining the live report producer.

The implementation contains 524 physical production lines after the standalone service bootstrap correction and 405 focused test lines. This exceeds the initial rough 300–400 production-line estimate. The size review was accepted before the real-data run because the retained code is confined to exact input validation, typed reconciliation, identity-only lookup projection, atomic replacement, and stale-state retention; SSP-2.2 retains the route, report registry, browser module, and visual presentation owners.

Accepted Product Contract

The physical scan uses the existing confined Projects directory owner and accepts only readable, non-symlink, non-hidden immediate directories below projects/. Those exact keys establish every report and lookup row. Project documents join independently through exact valid folder_path associations after the Manage manifest and subject-association generation and collection agree. Canonical Works join independently through projects/<project_folder> and project only work_id, project_folder, and series_ids; Studio catalogue/media retains the remaining Work fields.

Each live row carries exact folder presentation, ordered Project-document targets and links, semantic Work targets with current Series membership, canonical Series targets with exact Work IDs and counts, exceptional Series evidence, a distinct matched-Work count, and explicit reconciliation/document/Series states. The persisted folder lookup retains only the exact folder subject, semantic Work and Series targets with membership IDs, exact Project-document targets, generation receipts, and current/stale status. Presentation labels, routes, Work status, and media fields retain their existing owners.

On a successful run, a validated complete lookup replaces the prior file atomically. A failed write-enabled refresh retains the prior complete generation and relationships and atomically changes its status to stale with the failed time and bounded reason. A read-only run creates no lookup.

Real-Data Evidence

The accepted write-enabled run at 2026-08-05T14:34:21Z produced generation sha256:1f1780659a135713321091b4fd904f62149acc76b61deb851919b1d473b578d0 from subject generation sha256:259f140375197f541aa4e0bff7478339e9ad9e0807d33b50fced8bc801d81ef5. It completed in 109.701 ms and atomically published a current 206-folder lookup whose file SHA-256 is ad0a1790e18f4de48e64735e8d47364ddc3983cf4e947d56e09792f69c160ee6.

The current reconciliation matched 230 Project documents and all 1,940 canonical Works. Those Works produced 1,942 Series memberships across 143 canonical Series with complete Series evidence. Every recorded Project-document folder key and Work project_folder key matched the immediate physical inventory. The row states are 137 reconciled, 56 documents-only, seven Works-only, and six folder-only.

The projects/wa row contains 24 Works, two Project documents, and one Series 140 group containing all 24 Works. The eight current Works whose media resolves below projects/wa/ink/ remain within that first-level Work set because project_subfolder is outside the Project State projection.

Verification

  • Six focused tests pass for standalone service import, immediate-folder row ownership, independent joins, duplicate documents, all reconciliation states, incomplete and unknown Series evidence, identity-only lookup shape, ignored Work media/presentation fields, relationship-generation changes, atomic stale retention, and read-only failure behavior.
  • Thirty-six Project State, Projects-directory, authoring-subject, and sub-scope build tests pass together.
  • Explicit Python compilation and lint pass for the producer and focused tests.
  • The real lookup parses as JSON, carries 206 folder keys and a current status, shares the accepted generation, retains 24 projects/wa Works under Series 140, and contains semantic relationship fields under the accepted schema.
  • The lookup remains under the Git-ignored var/ owner, while public projection and tracked public data retain their existing products.
  • git diff --check passes.

Independent Review And Stop

The final source review found one entrypoint defect before publication: the first implementation relied on pytest-installed Studio import paths. The producer now invokes the existing Studio Python path bootstrap itself, and a subprocess test protects that standalone service boundary. The subsequent review found the scan, generation receipts, row origin, Work projection, Series counting, lookup projection, atomic replacement, and stale-state behavior aligned with the accepted SSP-2.1 contract.

SSP-2.2 retained ownership of the ordinary report host, management route, report registry and loader, automatic mount and explicit refresh, error/empty/busy presentation, and Folder-first table. SSP-2.3 retained grouping, search, sorting, TSV, and timestamp-prefixed Markdown copy. SSP-2.4 added no post-commit hooks. Its planned SSP-3 lookup consumer was later retired, so SSP-2.6 now removes that unused output instead of refreshing it during document builds.
